comment: Each case is a host with an independently characterised defect. The evidence predating this tool is in examples/usb/usb_audio_graph_test/transcript_hw_evkb.txt. Manifests carry max_packet_size_bytes because the judge requires it (added after this plan was written). Every case builds tools/uacvalidate/corpus/host, NOT the usb_audio_graph_test example: the example calls driver APIs that did not exist at these commits and cannot compile against them.

cases.witness_note: MUST be the 16-bit build (-DSTREAM_FORMAT_OUTPUT_1_RESOLUTION_BITS=16 -DSTREAM_FORMAT_INPUT_1_RESOLUTION_BITS=16). A 24-bit UAC1 witness makes uac1_find_alt miss and the host never claims -- that mis-read cost a published false accusation, retracted in 42a4a3b.

manifest.host_note: USBHost_t36 99cd466~1 -- before the UAC1 feedback read

cases.expect_reasoning: W1 WARN, not PASS or FAIL: W1 is PASS only within DRIFT_NOISE_FLOOR_PPM (1.0) and has no FAIL level at all, and an open loop at 85 ppm is 85x the floor. The fit lands because corrections come at the quantum/drift cadence -- seconds apart, far longer than vcdfill's 2 s minimum segment. R3 SKIP is structural: a 2-byte subslot has no spare lane to justify within.
cases.ground_truth: transcript_hw_evkb.txt: open loop at bias 0 drifts +85.0 ppm; block corrections at quantum/drift cadence.

manifest.host_note: USBHost_t36 1732ed3~1 -- before the HS feedback loop

cases.expect_reasoning: W1 WARN for the same reason as case A. The 9.6 s correction cadence in the ground truth is what makes the fit possible at all: segments that long clear vcdfill's 2 s / 8 point minimum with room to spare, so a SKIP here would mean the fill probe is missing, not that the drift is unmeasurable.
cases.ground_truth: transcript_hw_evkb.txt UAC2 P1: fill slope +119.3 B/s = +84.6 ppm, overflow corrections every ~9.6 s.

manifest.host_note: USBHost_t36 d370e80~1 -- before the alt-0 streaming gate

cases.ground_truth: transcript_hw_evkb.txt: the self-heal path zombie-streams the old ring at nominal into the device's alt 0.

stage.note: Same witness both phases: the trigger is re-enumeration under a streaming host, not a personality change. Capture is on phase 2 so it records the re-claim, which is where the pre-fix host streams into alt 0.

cases.ground_truth: 35b0cce is the fix commit: 'UAC2: left-justify samples within subslots; run test_pack in the gate'.
cases.skipped_reason: UN-STAGEABLE, and the plan's premise for this case is falsified. At 35b0cce~1 the driver's claim() begins `if (topo.bcd_adc != 0x0100) return false;` -- UAC1 only. It cannot claim a UAC2 device at all, so the right-justifying uac_pack16 was unreachable on hardware. Attempted 2026-08-05: host ran the full 180 s at `audio=none alt=-1 pkts/s=0` and the capture held zero state blocks (judge: INVALID, correctly). History order settles it: the fix 35b0cce is commit 588, UAC2 claim support 01c1cdd is 593 -- the bug was fixed five commits BEFORE the code path became reachable, so no commit in this tree has both. The design spec's original assumption was right: R3 has no historical negative and needs an injected one. See D2_right_justified_injected.
cases.expect_note: Expectations left exactly as derived. They are not reachable on hardware; that is a fact about the history, not a reason to soften the rule.

manifest.host_note: USBHost_t36 090eadb~1 -- device-swap wedge, after an FS->HS swap

cases.ground_truth: transcript_hw_evkb.txt: 'audio=ready uac2=0 alt=1 pkts/s=0' -- the claim and control sequence succeed while nothing is transmitted.

stage.note: Two-phase, one XTAG: phase 1 runs the UAC1 image uncaptured until the host claims and streams, then ends (SIGINT resets the xcore, which IS the disconnect); phase 2 brings the device back as UAC2 WITH the capture, host never reset. The plan's 'xrun the other image mid-capture' needs two XTAGs and is not stageable as written.

cases.expect_correction: The HOST behaviour reproduced exactly and is verified: through all 140 s of phase 2 the console read `audio=ready alt=1 pkts/s=0` with the FIFO frozen at 3854 -- the claim and control state survive while nothing is transmitted, matching the recorded `audio=ready uac2=0 alt=1 pkts/s=0`. What changed is the prediction about the TOOL, not the claim about the host. The plan expected per-rule SKIPs; the judge reports a capture-level INVALID, because the observer's emission is driven by packet arrival (uacvEmitBlock sits inside the decoupler's packet path) so a host that sends nothing produces a capture with zero state blocks. INVALID is correct for that input -- an empty capture genuinely could be a dead collector -- and exit 2 says nothing about the host, which is the honest answer. expect_no_pass keeps the assertion that actually matters: whatever shape the tool uses, it must never bless a host that transmitted nothing.
cases.finding: INSTRUMENT BLIND SPOT, found by this case. A device that is alive but receiving nothing is indistinguishable, in the capture, from a collector that failed -- both are zero blocks. The validator cannot therefore attribute this defect, only decline to rule. The fix is device-side: emit the state block on a timer independent of packet arrival, so 'device up, host silent' becomes a positive observation and R2/R3/R4 can SKIP with a named witness instead of the whole report going INVALID. Deferred to the observer branch; it changes the wire format's emission rule, not its layout.

manifest.host_note: USBHost_t36 master + defects/r3-right-justify.patch -- samples right-justified within the 4-byte subslot

cases.ground_truth: Injected because history has no reachable negative (see D_right_justified). The injection is the exact inverse of 35b0cce's fix: uac_pack16's 4-byte arm emits {lo,hi,0,0} instead of {0,0,lo,hi}. USB Audio Data Formats 2.0 2.3.1 requires the sample left-justified in the subslot, so the low byte must never be set -- R3's whole test.
cases.expect_reasoning: R3 FAIL, not SKIP: the tone keeps nonsilent_frames far above the vacuity floor, and a 4-byte subslot has the spare lane the structural SKIP is about. or_acc should come back with its low byte SET, which is the single boolean the whole justification finding rests on.

manifest.host_note: MIMXRT1170-EVKB, USBHost_t36 master -- clean-host regression, UAC1/FS, usb_audio_graph_test firmware

cases.expect_reasoning: The negative control. Every rule that fired against a defective host must come back clean here, or the corpus proves only that the tool can say FAIL. W1 PASS means inside DRIFT_NOISE_FLOOR_PPM (1.0); the closed-loop UAC1 soaks measured +0.10 and +0.24 ppm. R3 SKIP is structural, as in case A. Run fresh at master rather than reusing yesterday's UAC1 soak because today's ring-priming fix (3e66161) touched the FS path.
cases.ground_truth: UAC1 closed-loop soaks: +0.1 ppm (2026-08-04) and +0.238 ppm (21 min).
cases.host_firmware_reason: The corpus host streams FS at every historical corpus commit (case A: 1000 pkts/s) and streams HS at master (case D2: 8000 pkts/s), but on FS AT MASTER it claims the device, returns true from beginStreaming(), and then transmits nothing -- packets_sent flat, FIFO frozen full, no underruns, no transport errors. The repo's own UAC1 firmware on the identical witness at the same commit streams at pkts/s=999 with feedback polling healthy, so this is NOT a driver regression; it is something about the minimal host's interaction with master's FS path. OPEN QUESTION, recorded rather than papered over. It does not affect the historical cases, which all ran the corpus host successfully at their own commits; it only means the clean-FS control must use the shipping firmware -- which is arguably the better control anyway.

manifest.host_note: USBHost_t36 master (1f13bda) -- clean-host regression, UAC2/HS, judged from the 20-minute 1000 polls/s soak

cases.expect_reasoning: Reuses today's 1000 polls/s A/B soak rather than spending bench time on a second clean UAC2 run: same commit, same witness, same procedure, 20 minutes instead of 5. Provenance is in reuses_capture.
cases.ground_truth: transcript_uacv_1000polls_ab.txt: 9 PASS 0 FAIL, W1 -0.052 ppm, envelope 268 B.

manifest.host_note: USBHost_t36 master + defects/r4b-partial-frame.patch -- one extra byte per microframe

cases.expect_reasoning: R4b FAIL on not_multiple: 193 B is 6 audio frames of 32 B plus a stray byte. R4a should still PASS -- 193 is far inside the declared 800 B -- which is the point of having two rules: oversize and misaligned are different defects and only one is present.
cases.ground_truth: No host in this tree ever sent a partial frame, so R4b would otherwise ship having never fired on hardware. The device already tolerates this silently (decouple.xc, under a comment naming a bad driver); the injection makes that tolerance audible.

manifest.host_note: USBHost_t36 master + defects/w3-no-ema.patch -- servo chases the raw report

cases.expect_reasoning: The signature is the PAIRING: R1 PASS because the host is polling diligently, W3 WARN because it drifts anyway. R1 alone cannot see this defect, and that is precisely why W3 exists. W3 WARN means the residual exceeds DRIFT_NOISE_FLOOR_PPM (1.0); the shipping servo measures -0.05 ppm on the same bench. MAGNITUDE IS NOT PREDICTED: the historical +4.8 ppm was FS at 62.5 polls/s and this runs HS at 1000 polls/s. If the residual comes back inside the floor, that is a finding about raw-chasing at full poll rate, not a reason to move the floor.
cases.ground_truth: The EMA was never a standalone commit, so there is no parent to check out. Raw-chasing measured +4.8 ppm of sizing bias on this bench during the UAC1 feedback work -- a buffer excursion every ~45 min.
cases.attempt_1: FAILED TO REPRODUCE, and the reason is the finding. Removing the EMA alone, leaving the shipping 1000 polls/s reader, gave +0.389 ppm over 600 s -- 7x the shipping servo's -0.052 ppm but inside the 1 ppm floor, so W3 correctly PASSed. At one poll per frame the slew limiter (4 mHz/frame) IS the low-pass filter: each raw report is superseded before sizing can travel toward a rail. The historical +4.8 ppm was measured at 62.5 polls/s, where a report persists 16 frames and the asymmetry becomes bias. The INJECTION was wrong, not the expectation -- so the patch now reproduces the historical configuration (raw report AND 62.5 polls/s) rather than the expectation being softened.
cases.finding: The EMA's protective value shrinks as the poll rate approaches the device's report rate. Not a licence to drop it: the horizon invariant still guards the 62.5 polls/s FS reader, which has no such margin.

manifest.host_note: USBHost_t36 master + defects/r4a-oversize.patch -- microframe 0 carries 832 B against an advertised 800

cases.expect_reasoning: R4a FAIL if the oversize packet reaches the device's size histogram. It may not: a packet beyond wMaxPacketSize is a babble condition, and XUD may refuse or truncate it before lib_xua's decoupler counts anything. If the histogram never shows 832 the rule is UNPROVABLE ON THIS BENCH, which is a fact about the device stack, not a reason to weaken R4a. Recorded either way. R4b should stay PASS: 832 is 26 whole 32 B audio frames, so only the size rule has cause to fire.
cases.ground_truth: No host in this tree ever oversized a packet. This is the last rule with no hardware proof.
cases.attempt_1: 832 B EVERY frame. Two predictions falsified at once. (a) R4a is NOT structurally blocked: the prediction was that XUD would refuse a packet beyond wMaxPacketSize as babble before the decoupler could count it. False -- the histogram came back sizes [160, 192, 832], the device accepted and counted it. (b) But R4a never ran, because the manifest-contradiction guard fired first: mean packet 340.3 B against a 176.4 B prediction, 1.93x, and a mis-declared format is indistinguishable from an oversizing host in the mean, so the whole report was invalidated. The guard is correct -- it exists so a wrong manifest cannot produce a cited FAIL against a conformant host. The consequence is that R4a can only rule on oversize RARE or SMALL enough to keep the mean within one audio frame of prediction. The INJECTION was retuned, not the guard.
cases.finding: Two of the judge's safety mechanisms can pre-empt each other: the capture-level manifest guard runs before any rule, so a host whose defect is large enough to move the mean packet size gets an INVALID report rather than a cited FAIL naming the defect. Honest, but it means gross oversize is reported as 'cannot judge' rather than 'this host oversizes'. Worth revisiting only with a way to tell the two causes apart -- the capture alone cannot.
cases.result_note: R4a FAIL on 1308 packets of 832 B out of 1041200. R4b stayed PASS, so the two size rules are proven distinct in both directions (H proved the converse: misaligned but not oversized). UNREQUESTED BONUS FINDING: R3 also FAILed, or_acc=0xFFFF00E0 -- the low byte carrying data means the oversize packet knocked the device's subslot unpacking out of alignment, since the device's OUT geometry is sized for wMaxPacketSize. Collateral damage from the size defect, caught independently by a rule that knows nothing about packet size, and evidence the defect is materially harmful rather than merely nonconformant. W1/W3 SKIPped for want of a fittable segment: 86 dry-outs chopped the fill trace, which is the segmentation guard refusing to fit across corrections.
